newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar corrects down after recent rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar corrects down after recent rally.

text.p: London's spot August white sugar contract dominated overall market volume on Wednesday but price movements tracked the downward correction on the New York raws market, traders said.

Earlier, the August/October spread was the main feature of activity, trading between $10.20 and $10.50, but then contracted further to nearer $10.00 as profits were taken after August's rally earlier in the week.
Flat-price selling of the spot position also boosted volume, which by 1545 GMT stood at 1,998 lots. August trades alone accounted for 1,588 lots.

August, which broke through resistance at $317.50 on Tuesday to score a session high of $318.50, was down $1.70 at $316.70 and October down 50 cents at $307.00, the only contracts traded in any significant volume.
But traders said fears of supply tightness into the summer months could still push August higher and possibly to $323.00, an area of highs dating back to last October.
In Paris just 160 lots were traded, nearly all of which were also in August. The position was down $1.00 at $316.60, while October was untraded.
In other news, the French farm ministry cut its estimate for 1997 sugar beet sowings to 454,000 hectares from 455,000 hectares forecast last month.
